speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me which part of your body hurts and how long you've been limping?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain ever wake him up at night, and does he feel any discomfort in his left hip or groin area? I am also going to examine his hips for any limited range of motion, particularly internal rotation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That diagnosis of migraine is highly unlikely given your knee pain and limp, so we need to investigate the musculoskeletal system further. Does moving your left hip cause pain, and can you touch your toes or bring your knee to your chest without discomfort? REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: X-ray Left Hip Findings: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray findings of femoral head flattening and fragmentation are classic for Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of involvement, I will now proceed with the final determination. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
